title: Add NVTX ranges, runtime counters, microbench instrumentation and perf dashboard
author: Noah Chen
description:
Motivation: We need finer-grained visibility into per-component latency and GPU kernel hotspots in the serving runtime to make safe scheduling, KV cache, and batching optimizations. This PR adds NVTX ranges, lightweight runtime counters, and a microbenchmark instrumentation harness that feeds a Grafana perf dashboard for iterative performance work.

Summary of changes: 1) NVTX: add scoped NVTX ranges around key runtime phases (request de-queue, request parse, scheduler enqueue/dequeue, batch build, kernel launch, KV cache lookup/hit/miss, token decode/emit). Ranges are conditionally compiled and use low-overhead annotations to avoid perturbing microbenchmarks. 2) Counters: introduce atomic counters for request counts, KV cache hits/misses, batch sizes, and per-kernel invocation counts; exported via existing /metrics endpoint. 3) Microbench harness: new microbench CLI (tools/runtime-microbench) that can exercise single-request, batched, and KV-cache-heavy flows with warmup cycles and trace capture. 4) Perf dashboard: Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboards/runtime_profiling.json) with panels for NVTX-derived flamegraphs, KV cache hit-rate, batch size distributions, and kernel latency heatmaps. 5) Tests/docs: unit tests for counter correctness, end-to-end microbench CI job, and docs describing how to interpret NVTX ranges and use the dashboard.

Checklist:
- [x] NVTX annotations added around hot paths
- [x] Lightweight counters added and exposed to metrics endpoint
- [x] Microbench harness implemented and integrated into CI perf job
- [x] Grafana dashboard and dashboard README included
- [x] Unit tests for counters and small e2e microbench smoke test

Design notes: NVTX ranges are added at the C++ runtime boundary and in the scheduling layer; to avoid ABI or dependency changes the NVTX code is encapsulated behind a small shim (runtime/telemetry/nvtx_shim.h) that is a no-op when NVTX is not available. Counters are implemented with std::atomic<uint64_t> and registered with the existing metrics registry; we intentionally kept the metric names stable to avoid breaking downstream alerting. The microbench CLI supports output modes: human, json, and nvtx-trace (collects NVTX for later visualization).

Impact on performance: microbench numbers (included in PR comments) show <1% overhead in steady-state throughput when NVTX is enabled but without trace collection. With active tracing the overhead depends on collector configuration; we document recommended sampling for production. The added metrics and dashboard are intended to reduce iteration time for kernel optimization and batching policy tuning.

Backward compatibility and rollout: All instrumentation is opt-in via config flags (runtime.telemetry.enable_nvtx, runtime.telemetry.enable_counters). Default is off for NVTX tracing in hosted environments. Counters are enabled by default because they are low-overhead. We included rollout notes and a migration plan in docs/telemetry/README.md.

Related linear tasks: ENG-3174 (runtime profiling pass), ENG-3189 (KV cache perf investigation).

review_comments: Elena Park: Please add NVTX ranges around the batch packing path; those are where we saw variability in the canary runs. Also prefer a scoped RAII helper over raw begin/end pairs.

Noah Chen: Addressed — added ScopedNvtxRange helper and moved batch packing annotations into scheduler::build_batch(). Updated comments and added unit test that validates range nesting in the microbench trace output.

Miguel Torres: Metrics look good. Two requests: (1) make sure metric names use the "runtime_" prefix for consistency, (2) add a histogram for batch sizes rather than only counters.

Noah Chen: (1) prefixed metric names, (2) added batch_size histogram exported via the metrics registry. Updated test coverage.

Svetlana Ivanova: CI perf job failed once due to flaky GPU allocation in the runner; suggest adding a retry wrapper to the microbench CI step.

Noah Chen: Added retry with exponential backoff for the CI runner and a jitter cap. Re-ran CI; green now.

release_notes: Add optional NVTX tracing and lightweight runtime counters to aid kernel, scheduling and KV-cache performance investigations. Includes microbench harness and Grafana dashboard for observability.
